title: What Was a Reform?
definition: A deliberate change to a rule, institution or practice.
content:
A reform changes how something is organized or done. Colonial officials could seek more government income, encourage production or change the organization of trade. These are aims: what a policy was intended to do. The word reform does not prove that a change was fair or helpful to everyone. We still need to investigate its operation and effects.

Use a three-part journal: aim, method and effect. The aim describes the intended change. The method describes how authorities tried to bring it about. The effect concerns what followed for particular people or activities. These parts can differ. A policy might raise income while placing burdens on producers. An official statement helps establish an aim, but accounts of affected people help investigate experience. The journal is a modern teaching tool, not a surviving colonial report. Your task is to compare evidence rather than praise every new rule.

Open the three clues. Choose the explanation supported by the evidence. Use Explain if you need help, then return to your decision.
clues: What did officials intend to change?
How did they try to bring about that change?
Calling a policy a reform does not prove equal benefits.
task: What should we investigate before calling a reform helpful to everyone?
Evidence of its effects on different people
Only its name
Only the date of announcement
Only the word reform
reason: What did officials intend to change? How did they try to bring about that change? Calling a policy a reform does not prove equal benefits.

title: Ideas and Practical Production
definition: An organization concerned with economic knowledge and activity.
content:
Under Jose Basco y Vargas, the Sociedad Economica de los Amigos del Pais was established in 1781. A modern historical study places it within efforts to encourage agriculture and industry. Agriculture concerns growing crops and raising animals; industry includes making and processing goods. Practical knowledge could be used to improve production.

Keep the institution separate from a promise of instant prosperity. Establishing a society does not prove that all farmers received help or that every proposal was carried out. The research also describes periods when the society was inactive, so do not assume continuous success. Imagine a proposal card beside a record of a completed activity. The proposal shows an intention; the activity record is needed to investigate what was actually done. These example cards are teaching models. Later achievements must keep their own dates instead of being moved back to the founding year.

Open the three clues. Choose the explanation supported by the evidence. Use Explain if you need help, then return to your decision.
clues: The society was established in 1781 under Basco.
Agriculture and industry were concerns of economic development.
Founding an institution does not prove every proposal was carried out.
task: What can the founding date establish?
When the society was established
That all later projects happened that year
That every farmer received help
That activity never paused
reason: The society was established in 1781 under Basco. Agriculture and industry were concerns of economic development. Founding an institution does not prove every proposal was carried out.

title: Income and Burdens Could Coexist
definition: A demand or difficulty placed on someone.
content:
The tobacco monopoly offers a concrete example of a government policy affecting production. Established in 1782, it sought government revenue. The National Tobacco Administration historical account describes required planting and quotas, as well as complaints and abuses in affected areas. A quota was a required amount to produce. These details help explain why an income policy could create difficulties for producers.

Distinguish an official goal from a household experience. An official could count income, while a farmer faced a production requirement. Those are different measures of an effect. Do not assume that every region grew tobacco or that each household experienced the policy in exactly the same way. Ask about the place, time and people in the account. Tobacco is a historical example here, not an invitation to use it. No activity asks you to grow, buy or try tobacco, and the game gives no points for producing it.

Open the three clues. Choose the explanation supported by the evidence. Use Explain if you need help, then return to your decision.
clues: A quota required an amount of production.
Government income alone does not measure household wellbeing.
task: Which comparison helps explain the monopoly?
Compare government revenue with demands on producers
Treat revenue as every households happiness
Assume all regions grew the crop
Ignore all production requirements
reason: Revenue was a government aim. A quota required an amount of production. Government income alone does not measure household wellbeing.

title: A Charter Created an Institution
definition: An official document establishing an organization or its authority.
content:
A royal charter dated 10 March 1785 established the Compania de Filipinas, often called the Royal Company of the Philippines. The University Complutense of Madrid preserves a catalogue record for this printed document. This is an example of creating an institution through royal authority. The date and kind of document help us identify an official step in organizing economic activity.

A charter and a record of everyday trade answer different questions. The charter establishes an official authorization; it does not by itself show every shipment, profit or household experience. We are examining the catalogue description, not pretending to have read every clause of the document. Do not say that this institution instantly replaced every earlier trade connection. In Mission 1 you saw that the Manila-Acapulco route continued until 1815. New institutions and older practices could exist during overlapping periods. Keep both sets of dates in your journal.

Open the three clues. Choose the explanation supported by the evidence. Use Explain if you need help, then return to your decision.
clues: A charter is an official step establishing an organization.
Authorization alone does not establish every result of its operation.
task: What does the dated charter directly support?
An official step establishing the company
Every household becoming wealthy
Every shipment reaching its destination
All earlier trade ending immediately
reason: The charter is dated 10 March 1785. A charter is an official step establishing an organization. Authorization alone does not establish every result of its operation.

title: Build a Fair Reform Report
definition: A judgement made using clear questions and evidence.
content:
Compare the society, monopoly and company through the same questions. What was established or changed? What method was used? What effects are supported? An organization concerned with economic knowledge, a production monopoly and a royal charter are different kinds of evidence. They should not be treated as three identical solutions or as proof that every community experienced the same change.

For your report, choose one example and write an aim or official step beside a supported effect or an unanswered question. Mark the source for each statement. If you have only a founding date, do not invent a family story to supply the missing experience. If a source describes a burden, do not erase it because officials had a development goal. A fair judgement can recognize an intended improvement while examining limits and unequal effects. Later missions will investigate new ideas and grievances; you do not need to claim that one reform made every later event inevitable.

Open the three clues. Choose the explanation supported by the evidence. Use Explain if you need help, then return to your decision.
clues: Use the same questions for different examples.
Keep an official step separate from evidence of an effect.
A development goal does not cancel evidence of burdens.
task: Which report makes a fair judgement?
It separates aims, official steps and supported effects
It assumes all reforms helped everyone
It removes every complaint
It invents effects from a founding date
reason: Use the same questions for different examples. Keep an official step separate from evidence of an effect. A development goal does not cancel evidence of burdens.
